Step 4 needs no file edits and no new commands. The stats are already in hand. The backlog has 26 open items, which is at or above 20, so I present the triage proposal (rubric steps 1-4, read-only) as part of this completion batch. I then continue to step 5 without waiting, because the triage never blocks completion.

**Edits:** none. **Commands:** none for step 4. Step 5 starts next with `uv run ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/scripts/deferral_scan.py scan specs/plans/12-dock-alerts.md specs/dock-alerts.md`.

**Message to my partner:**

Plan 12 (dock-alerts) is executed and marked up. Two items were deferred into `specs/deferred_items.md` under `12-dock-alerts`.

**Backlog health:** Deferred backlog: 26 open, 51 ever closed (closure rate 66%), aged >45d: 0. The oldest open item is 35d (3-station-geocoding). The age spread is 12 items at 0-14d, 12 at 15-30d and 2 at 31-45d. That is above the 20-item volume threshold, so here is the triage proposal.

No item is past the aged-tail gate yet. Two cross 45 days soon: the geocoder cache item on 2026-11-19 and the API rate-limit item on 2026-11-22. The three 5-rebalance-trucks quick-fixes follow on 2026-11-28. If they are still open then, they will block the merge/PR at finishing.

I sorted by each item's recorded `Size:`. I did not check for Retire or Hold candidates, because I have no tools this turn and no item records an unmet external condition. I propose no `→ triggered` notes.

**Quick fix (12), done directly:**
- Dock status and alerts:
  - Poll interval is a magic number in two files (9-dock-status, 10-30)
  - Status history table has no index on `dock_id` (9-dock-status, 10-30)
  - Alert threshold is a constant in `alerts/notify.py`, not config (12-dock-alerts, 11-09)
- Trucks and routes:
  - Truck route export drops stops with no free docks (5-rebalance-trucks, 10-14)
  - Route CSV has no header row (5-rebalance-trucks, 10-14)
  - No test for a truck that starts with an empty load (5-rebalance-trucks, 10-14)
- Reports:
  - Weekly report counts out-of-service docks twice (7-fleet-reports, 10-22)
  - Report job does not retry on a status API timeout (7-fleet-reports, 10-22)
- Other:
  - Geocoder cache never expires for moved stations (3-station-geocoding, 10-05)
  - Station pin colors fail the contrast check (6-station-map, 10-19)
  - Notice emails have no unsubscribe link (8-rider-notices, 10-26)
  - Battery readings above 100% are stored as sent (10-battery-telemetry, 11-03)

**Plan (10), ranked:**
1. **Public status API has no per-key rate limit** (4-api-limits, 10-08). It is the oldest and the only item that exposes the service to outside abuse.
2. **Map group, one plan** (6-station-map, 10-19). It covers tiles refetched on every refresh, a closed station shown as open for up to 5 minutes, and untranslated pin tooltips. All three touch the map refresh path.
3. **Report group** (7-fleet-reports, 10-22). It covers the PDF layout breaking above 200 stations and report totals not checked against the status feed.
4. **Notices group** (8-rider-notices, 10-26). It covers hard-coded two-language text and batching that is untested above 500 riders.
5. **Telemetry batches are not deduplicated on retry** (10-battery-telemetry, 11-03). It is newer, but duplicates corrupt stored data.
6. **Alert emails repeat when a dock flaps** (12-dock-alerts, 11-09). It is today's final-review finding and is user-visible. Its closure condition, one alert per dock per hour with a test, is already written. Pairing it with the threshold-to-config quick-fix keeps the work in one place.

**Design (4), ranked:**
1. **A dock with a stuck sensor reports free slots forever** (9-dock-status, 10-30). It is the oldest, and it undermines what the alerts rely on.
2. **Quiet hours ignore the rider's time zone** (8-rider-notices, 10-26). It is a rider-facing correctness bug.
3. **Rebalance targets ignore weekday demand** (5-rebalance-trucks, 10-14). It is the oldest of the four but the least urgent.
4. **No alert when a bike battery stays low for 3 days** (10-battery-telemetry, 11-03). It is a new feature that builds on the telemetry dedup plan.

**Retire / Hold:** none proposed. `/deferred` can check retire candidates with a concrete grep or `git log -S` per item.

`/deferred` acts on a selection from this list. The simplest first pick is the 12 quick-fixes, since the three oldest are about to age out. Nothing here blocks completion, so I am continuing to step 5: the deferral scan, retiring the plan and writing the history entry.
